newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds push higher at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds push higher at close.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed solidly higher Tuesday after a late spurt of buying driven by gains on Wall Street, dealers said.

"The market started out with short positions and played catch-up at the end, closing very firm," a dealer at a leading local brokerage said. "I would say these gains are spurred by the recent fall in the U.S. long bond yield below 6.6 percent, and the record set today by the Dow."
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 jumped $1.20 to 121.7. Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 95.
"The market's in a very good mood and nobody wants to miss the winning wave," another dealer said. "We saw more movement than we expected ahead of the holiday tomorrow."
Markets will be closed for Argentina's Independence Day on Wednesday.
